title: Photography and Hyper-Realism
answer: Synthetic portraiture, lighting rigs, upscaling, product mockups and virtual location scouting.

children.name: Synthetic Portraiture
children.blurb: Synthetic portraiture is the making of human or human-like likenesses with generative image models, whether the subject is a real person, a composite, or a wholly invented face.

children.name: Lighting Rigs and Relighting
children.blurb: Lighting rigs and relighting cover the setup and control of light in a photograph or a rendered image, and the later adjustment of that light after the fact.

children.name: Upscaling and Noise Reduction
children.blurb: Upscaling and noise reduction cover the post processing steps that take a finished or nearly finished image and make it larger, cleaner, or both.

children.name: Product and Fashion Mockups
children.blurb: Product and fashion mockups cover the generated or composited imagery that stands in for a photograph of an object or garment before the real shoot happens.

children.name: Virtual Location Scouting
children.blurb: Virtual location scouting is the practice of finding, generating, or assembling a plausible place for a shoot before anyone travels there.

sections.body: Photography and hyper-realism covers the use of generative models to produce images that read as photographs, and to repair or extend real photographs after capture. Synthetic portraiture builds faces and bodies from text prompts or reference shots, with control over pose, age and expression. Lighting rigs and relighting let a model change the direction, colour and softness of light on an existing subject, which is the part that most often decides whether an image looks real. Upscaling and noise reduction reconstruct detail in low resolution or high ISO files, and product and fashion mockups place garments and objects into scenes that never existed. Virtual location scouting generates plausible backdrops and camera angles before anyone travels to a shoot.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Faces are largely solved at small sizes and in good light, and viewers routinely fail to pick synthetic portraits from real ones in controlled tests. Hands, teeth, ears, jewellery and text remain weak points, and skin at full resolution still shows a plastic smoothness that retouchers notice immediately. Relighting works well for diffuse, frontal light and degrades with hard shadows, mirrors and translucent materials. Upscaling invents detail rather than recovering it, which matters when the file is evidence rather than decoration. Product mockups are good enough for internal review and social posts but rarely for print catalogues, and generated locations can drift in perspective and geography across a sequence of shots.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Start with Synthetic Portraiture for the core problem of making a person who was never there, including identity, consent and the tells that give a generated face away. Lighting Rigs and Relighting is the companion piece, since light placement is what separates a convincing portrait from a flat one, and it applies equally to generated and photographed subjects. Upscaling and Noise Reduction sits downstream of both, dealing with what happens when a good image is too small or too grainy, and with the ethics of adding detail that was not captured. Product and Fashion Mockups takes the same techniques into commercial work, where the demands are consistency across a set and accurate representation of a real object. Virtual Location Scouting closes the section by moving the camera itself, generating places and angles so that a shoot can be planned, or faked, before anyone leaves the desk.
